activity.notes: Belisarius was Justinian I's preeminent general. His major command career began in the Persian war in the late 520s, included the reconquests of Vandal North Africa and Ostrogothic Italy, and ended with a final field engagement defending Constantinople in 559. ATLAS records 529–559 as a representative military-activity span, not as an assertion of uninterrupted annual office; periods of recall, disgrace and retirement are preserved by that distinction.

sources.title: Belisarius, c. 500–565 CE — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: Oxford Classical Dictionary identifies Belisarius as Justinian's famous general, traces his command career from the Persian campaigns through Africa and Italy, and records his final defense of Constantinople against the Cutrigurs in 559.

sources.title: General of the East — Belisarius & Antonina — Oxford Academic
sources.citation_text: Oxford's modern study of Belisarius describes his rapid advancement in the late 520s to Duke of Mesopotamia and General of the East and his command at Dara in 530.
